cross_case_findings: Rates = sector_delta * 512 / (1048576 * window_s). Logical-to-physical write ratio = logical_write_bytes / (physical_write_sector_delta * 512). Completion_ratio = completion_ms / baseline_completion_ms, so larger means slower.
Full-pressure percentages = 100 * delta_us / (window_s * 1000000). These measure full-stall time, not device utilization; shorter windows can raise the percentage for the same stall duration.

C4W1S1, C4W1S7, C4W1S13 and C4W1S19 show stalled checkpoints, long readers and copy traffic. Reader-pinned WAL is plausible, but aggregate device counters cannot assign I/O to copying or SQLite; their completion ratio is only 1.025000.

C4W1S2, C4W1S8, C4W1S14 and C4W1S20 show 300 MiB available, active swapping and substantial memory full, with completion ratio 2.250000. Local memory pressure is directly supported; absence of 429 does not exclude additional provider latency.

C4W1S3, C4W1S9, C4W1S15 and C4W1S21 show provider 429s, quick sends and negligible local pressure, with completion ratio 2.125000. Retry timing must establish how much of the excess is provider throttling.

C4W1S4, C4W1S10, C4W1S16 and C4W1S22 show eight busy errors in DELETE mode and completion ratio 1.050000. Contention is evidenced, but the blocking transaction is unidentified. The remaining eight cases are healthy in the observed windows.

Logical-to-physical write ratios span 1.000000 through 5.000000 across both slow and healthy cases. These are the requested logical/physical direction, not physical/logical amplification. Buffering, coalescing, differing counter scopes and unrelated copy traffic prevent direct attribution.

Physical read bytes are exactly one quarter of physical write bytes in every fixture. Throughput alone does not establish saturation or read purpose; short local windows versus longer completion measurements also limit causal attribution. This synthetic set cannot establish a real-agent capacity limit.
